import pandas as pd

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length3_75/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length3_75/training_1.csv"

df0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)
df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)

# Step 1: Join Source3_75_0 and Source3_75_1 on 'city'
joined = pd.merge(df0, df1[['city', 'type']], on='city', how='inner')

# Step 2: Group by city and type, aggregate average fare
grouped = joined.groupby(['city', 'type'], as_index=False)['fare'].mean()

# Step 3: The target schema is ['city': string, 'type': string, 'fare': float]
# Ensure correct types
grouped['city'] = grouped['city'].astype(str)
grouped['type'] = grouped['type'].astype(str)
grouped['fare'] = grouped['fare'].astype(float)

# Save to target path
target_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_75/target_multisource.csv"
grouped.to_csv(target_path, index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_75/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_75/training_1.csv", index_col=0)

# Join on city (inner join)
joined = pd.merge(source0, source1, how='inner', on='city')

# Group by city (primary key) and type, aggregate average fare
# But target FD says city -> type, fare, so type is functionally dependent on city
# So grouping by city only is enough, and type can be taken as first (all same per city)
agg = joined.groupby('city').agg(
    fare=('fare', 'mean'),
    type=('type', 'first')
).reset_index()

# Reorder columns to match target schema: ['city', 'type', 'fare']
agg = agg[['city', 'type', 'fare']]

# Write output
agg.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_75/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
